# Money questions we saved

Short answers from a personal finance website's FAQ, printed for the file.

## Will renters insurance cover my stolen laptop?

Renters insurance generally covers the theft of your belongings, including things taken from a car, up to the policy's limits. Read your own policy for its limits and for what you must do to file a claim.

## How does an employer 401(k) match work?

A match is extra money your employer adds when you contribute to your 401(k), usually up to a set share of your pay. It is part of your benefits, so ask your human resources office for your plan's rate and the schedule on which it becomes yours.

## Should I pay off debt or build savings first?

Both matter. Paying off high-interest debt saves money, while savings keep you from borrowing again. Many people do a little of each at the same time.

## Who inherits my retirement accounts?

Retirement accounts are handled separately from the rest of your property. Check the plan's paperwork, or ask an estate planning lawyer about your situation.

## Can I deduct my home office?

Some people who work from home can deduct part of their housing costs. The rules are strict and depend on how you earn your income, so ask a tax professional.

## How do I stop paying mortgage insurance?

Ask your lender when it can be removed. Lenders have their own procedures, and you may need a new appraisal of the home.

## How often should I check my credit report?

You can get a free copy of your report from each of the three bureaus every year. Look for accounts you do not recognize and for errors in your personal details.

## What counts as an emergency expense?

A car repair you need to get to work, an urgent medical bill, or a broken furnace in winter. A sale, a vacation or a gift is not an emergency.

## How much can I contribute to my retirement accounts?

The limits depend on the type of account and on your age, and they change from year to year. Check the IRS website for the current numbers before you contribute.

## Can I take money out of my 401(k) early?

You can usually take money out early, but it is often taxed and may carry a penalty. Think twice, and ask a tax professional before you do.

## Do I lose my HSA money at the end of the year?

Rules for health accounts differ. Some let unspent money carry forward and others do not, so check which kind of account you have.

## Why was my health insurance claim denied?

Claims are denied for many reasons, such as missing paperwork or a service the plan does not cover. Read the denial letter, call the plan, and ask about an appeal if you disagree.
